subject: biology
title: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria
key_idea: Bacteria reproduce quickly, and mutations can make a strain resistant to an antibiotic. Natural selection then lets the resistant bacteria survive and reproduce, so the resistant strain spreads. This is evolution that can be seen happening. Using antibiotics carefully slows it down.

blocks.text: Antibiotic resistance is natural selection in bacteria. This section covers the steps.

items.meaning: When bacteria are not killed by an antibiotic. A resistant strain survives treatment with it.
A variety of a type of bacterium, with different genes from other strains.
A strain of bacteria that is resistant to antibiotics.

items: Bacteria can evolve rapidly because they **reproduce at a fast rate**.
**Mutations** of bacterial pathogens produce new strains.
Some strains might be resistant to antibiotics, so they are not killed.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of how antibiotic resistance evolves in order.
steps: Variation in the population of bacteria is caused by mutation
The population of bacteria is exposed to the antibiotic
Bacteria with the mutation for resistance are more likely to survive
The mutation for resistance is passed on to offspring, so the resistant strain increases

items: Mutation gives a resistant strain. Natural selection makes it common.
Non-resistant bacteria are killed. Resistant bacteria survive and reproduce.
Bacteria evolve quickly because they reproduce quickly.

sections.heading: Why it matters and what it shows

blocks.text: Resistance is a problem for medicine. It is also evidence for evolution.

items: The resistant strain spreads because people are **not immune** to it and there is no effective treatment.
Resistance is **evidence for evolution**. It shows natural selection happening in a short time, so it supports Darwin's theory.
Evolution is easier to study in bacteria than with fossils. Bacteria have a short life cycle, they are still evolving, and scientists can study their DNA.
Making new antibiotics is costly and slow. It is unlikely to keep up with new resistant strains.
Resistant strains spread because there is no effective treatment.
Antibiotic resistance supports the theory of evolution by natural selection.

blocks.text: Resistance cannot be stopped, but it can be slowed. Most methods mean fewer bacteria are exposed to antibiotics or fewer survive.

items: Doctors should **not prescribe antibiotics inappropriately**. Mild bacterial infections get better with the immune system, and antibiotics do not kill viruses.
Patients should **complete the course** of antibiotics. All the bacteria are killed, so none survive to mutate and form resistant strains.
Restrict the **agricultural use** of antibiotics, so fewer bacteria are exposed. Antibiotics from farm animals pass into the environment, where bacteria in water or on land become resistant.
To limit the spread of a resistant strain, isolate patients who have it and wash hands.
Do not use antibiotics for viral or mild infections.
Finish the course so no bacteria survive to mutate.

checks.q: Explain how a population of bacteria can become resistant to an antibiotic.
checks.a: A mutation makes some bacteria resistant. The antibiotic kills the non-resistant bacteria, but the resistant bacteria survive and reproduce. They pass on the resistance, so the population becomes resistant. This is natural selection.

checks.q: Why should a patient complete their course of antibiotics?
checks.a: So that all the bacteria are killed and none survive to mutate and form resistant strains.

checks.q: Why do doctors avoid giving antibiotics to treat a cold?
checks.a: A cold is caused by a virus and antibiotics do not kill viruses. Unnecessary use increases the chance of resistant strains.

worked_example.question:
Most of the world's production of antibiotics is used in farming.
Antibiotics are given to animals to prevent the spread of disease.

Explain how the widespread use of antibiotics in farming is a threat to human life.
answer_points: Antibiotic is passed into the environment in animal faeces, urine or sewage.
Bacteria in water or on land become antibiotic resistant.
Some of these bacteria are human pathogens.
They cause human diseases that now cannot be cured because they are antibiotic resistant.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link in the chain.

worked_example.question:
In 2017, a new strain of Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteria was discovered that was resistant to 26 different antibiotics.

Explain how Klebsiella pneumoniae bacteria developed resistance to antibiotics.
answer_points: By natural selection or evolution.
A mutation in the bacterium, or variation in the population.
Only the resistant bacteria survived treatment with antibiotics, or they survive when people do not finish the course.
The resistant bacteria reproduce or divide.
Offspring inherit the resistance, and the process repeats, increasing the level of resistance.
worked_example.tip: Any four of the five points score one mark each.

worked_example.question:
Antibiotic resistance is an increasing problem worldwide.
Explain how bacteria become resistant to antibiotics.
answer_points: Random mutations occur in some of the bacteria.
There is genetic variation in the ability of bacteria to survive antibiotic treatment.
Bacteria with antibiotic resistance survive and reproduce.
They pass on the resistance allele to their offspring.
The resistance allele increases in frequency in the population.
This is natural selection: the bacteria become better adapted to the new environment.

worked_example.question:
Some antibiotics are becoming less effective at controlling bacterial infections.
Explain how bacteria have evolved so that antibiotics are less effective.
answer_points: A mutation in some bacteria gives resistance to the antibiotic.
Only the resistant bacteria survive.
The resistant bacteria reproduce.
They pass on the alleles for resistance.
The resistant bacteria increase in number, so most of the disease is caused by resistant strains.
